item.title: Zojo-ji Temple — Guide
item.description: Zojo-ji, at the foot of Tokyo Tower in Shiba-koen, is one of Tokyo’s most important and historic temples, with a striking juxtaposition of old and new. Founded in the fourteenth century and later chosen as the family temple of the ruling Tokugawa shogunate, it was once an enormous temple complex, and several shoguns are buried in its mausoleum. Its imposing main gate, the Sangedatsumon, dates from 1622 and is one of the oldest wooden structures in Tokyo, having survived wars and disasters.
